extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting manuscripts to peer-reviewed journals (medical/academic researchers), especially VSI authors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting a response letter and revised manuscript when addressing peer reviewers' comments after journal peer review; includes tone, format, and specific content to include. Focused on medical/academic journal submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter to the editor and reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Please start the response letter with thanks to the editors and reviewers, and show that you have sincerely taken full account of all the reviewers' comments. Provide an overview of the changes, new data, and new analyses performed in response to the most essential comments of all the reviewers. Then quote the full set of reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with thanks; include an overview summarizing key revisions and any new analyses or data; include the full reviews (so reviewers/editors can see original comments alongside responses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be polite and respectful
rubrics_metrics.description: As an author, you do not have to agree with every feedback, but politeness will help obtain a favorable decision. Do not attack the reviewers or question their motives, expertise, or intellectual aptitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat reviewers as you would like to be treated. Even if reviewers are rude, remain polite; if you disagree, respond tactfully (e.g., explain that 'Our manuscript has been reviewed by a native English speaker, and revised to improve readability.'). If you believe a reviewer has conflict of interest, malicious intent, or discriminatory attitude, report that separately to the editor-in-chief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond point-by-point to each and every comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond point-by-point to each and every comment raised by all reviewers. If you agree with the comment, acknowledge it and mention the changes you made. If you disagree, provide a reasonable explanation as to why you did not make the suggested change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not repeat thanks in every response. If additional work or experiments are recommended, do them if possible; otherwise tactfully explain why the additional work cannot be performed. Providing an authors' document with an overview and point-by-point responses shows the editor you carefully considered and addressed each criticism, aiding editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the response self-contained
rubrics_metrics.description: Show exactly how you revised the manuscript so that the reviewer does not need to go back to the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make your changes stand out by using different typefaces, colors, and indentations for the three different elements: the reviewer comment, your response, and the change made in the manuscript. Highlight changes for better understanding. You can show both the original and revised versions of altered paragraphs to make it easy for the editor/reviewer to see how you dealt with the criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay optimistic and avoid emotional responses
rubrics_metrics.description: If you feel that you received a harsh review, give yourself time to digest before attempting to respond. Don't send a letter in anger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read all comments carefully before answering. You can vent privately by drafting a scathing response you will not send, then write a professional version. If you find contradictory comments by different reviewers, stick with what you think is more appropriate (reviewers are blind to each other and may change opinions after seeing your response).

rubrics_metrics.name: Check repeatedly for any mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: The best way to write a good manuscript is to rewrite repeatedly and ask other co-authors to cross-check the revised manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofread and revise multiple times; have co-authors review revisions before resubmission to catch errors and improve clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Think from the reviewers' perspective and persuade with evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must think from the reviewers' perspective, communicate effectively, and persuade the reviewers with evidence that the manuscript is good enough for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate reviewer concerns, provide clear explanations or data to address criticisms, and structure responses to convince reviewers and editors of the manuscript's merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defend incorrect comments with sound scientific rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors have the right to alter their manuscript as per reviewers' recommendations or defend themselves against incorrect comments with sound scientific rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When disagreeing, supply clear, evidence-based arguments explaining why a suggested change was not made; remain professional and avoid attacking the reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: When misunderstanding occurs, revise the manuscript for clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reviewer failed to understand something, it is most likely because you failed to explain it clearly. Rewrite the paragraphs in question to convey your point clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume misunderstanding reflects lack of clarity rather than reviewer incompetence; revise text to be clearer for readers and reviewers alike, rather than simply arguing that the reviewer is wrong.
